headline: The North Star must grow 4.5x on a base that is partly noise

blocks.proof: 28k to 125k net level-ups by 30 June, while clients grow only 2.1x (598k to 1.25M).
blocks.implication: Existing clients must climb faster and drop less.

blocks.proof: Balance-linked points make clients bounce across levels.
blocks.implication: Part of the North Star is noise.

blocks.proof: Targeted communication: 24.6% vs 13% enrolment; 63% vs 34% reward choice.
blocks.implication: Execution, not product, made the gap.

annotation: Finance does not yet see CM3 value, so proving impact matters as much as growth.
source: Source: case study brief; 28k counted since the silent launch.
notes: The North Star has to grow 4.5x while the client base only doubles. So growth cannot come from enrolment alone; existing clients must level up faster and drop less.

The most important signal is the drops. Because points depend on balances, every 500k CZK or a closed term deposit moves points. Clients near a threshold bounce up and down without changing behaviour, and their savings rate bounces with them. So part of our North Star is balance noise.
The pilot shows execution matters: targeted communication almost doubled enrolment. And Finance does not yet see the value, which makes proof a survival issue for the programme.
